title: Allow pagination to hide when there is only one page
body: Quite a simple one, when there is only one page hide the pagination else it looks a little silly just sitting there on it's own as a single box saying "1".

comments.body: Hi, you can do a simple hide pagination widget: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/1049#issuecomment-222927757
Ah will need to take a look at that thanks
Okay, that works, but seem really messy to have to add a custom widget just to hide the pagination on single page results.
I agree with @Sammaye this should be easier to achieve.

@rayrutjes We are open to discussion for an API that does not requires adding more classnames. The issue is that the more state we inline into the classes API, the less easy it is to document it.

Also utlimately this is a design decision but if you hide the pagination when there's only one page, you do provide less context for the user. If there's no pagination on a webpage (or if the pagination is hidden/shown given some context I do not decide), then the user might think "Well, maybe there's more result, maybe that the only page, but I can't tell it because I don't know how this page is built".
TBH showing a lonely "1" on the page is actually proven (form my own testing) less contextually useful to the end user

Found another solution - I'm using Vue, but should be doable across the board. 1. Use ais-stats to get number of pages ```vue ``` 2. As you run the function to generate the result text, you can decide to show the pagination ```js getResultText(nbHits, page, nbPages) { // Decide to show pagination if (nbPages > 1) eventBus.isShowingPagination = true // Return text let text = '' if (nbHits === 0) text = `W: No products found` if (nbHits === 1) text = `W: ${ nbHits } product found` if (nbHits > 1) text = `W: ${ nbHits } products found` if (nbPages > 1) text += ` - Page ${ page + 1 } of ${ nbPages }` return text } ``` 3. Now you can show/hide your pagination conditionally ```vue ``` Best of luck
